subject: Biology
title: Synaptic Transmission: Electrical vs. Chemical Synapses
learningObjectives: Differentiate Electrical and Chemical synapses structurally, kinetically, and functionally
Describe the role of Connexons and gap junctions in electrical synapses
Trace the molecular cascade of chemical synaptic transmission: Ca2+ influx, Synaptotagmin, and SNARE-mediated exocytosis
content:
A Synapse is a specialized functional junction mediating signal transfer between a neuron and a target cell (another neuron, muscle fiber, or gland).

```
                             SYNAPSE TAXONOMY
                                     │
         ┌───────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                       ▼
  ELECTRICAL SYNAPSES                                     CHEMICAL SYNAPSES
  ├── Direct cytoplasmic contact via Connexons             ├── Separated by Synaptic Cleft (20–50 nm)
  ├── Gap Junction Channels (1.5 nm)                      ├── Mediated by Neurotransmitters
  ├── Bi-directional, extremely rapid (<0.2 ms)           ├── Unidirectional, slower (0.5–2.0 ms)
  └── Rare in human CNS (Heart, Smooth Muscle)            └── Predominant type in Human CNS & PNS
```

### 5.1 Molecular Cascade of Chemical Synaptic Transmission

```
                     CHEMICAL SYNAPTIC CASCADE
                     
   Action Potential arrives at Presynaptic Terminal Button
                             │
   Opens Voltage-Gated Ca²⁺ Channels ──► Ca²⁺ INFLUX into Presynaptic Cytosol
                                             │
   Ca²⁺ binds Synaptotagmin ──► Triggers SNARE-mediated Vesicle Fusion
                                             │
   Exocytosis of Neurotransmitter into Synaptic Cleft
                                             │
   Binds Ligand-Gated Receptors on Postsynaptic Membrane
                             │
   Opens Ion Channels ──► Produces EPSP or IPSP
```

- **Synaptotagmin**: Primary presynaptic $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ sensor.
- **SNARE Complex**: v-SNAREs (Synaptobrevin) on vesicles bind t-SNAREs (Syntaxin, SNAP-25) on the presynaptic membrane to drive vesicle fusion.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Tetanus & Botulinum Neurotoxin Cleavage of SNAREs
conceptBreakdown.explanation: Botulinum toxin (Botox) cleaves SNAP-25/Syntaxin at the NMJ, preventing ACh release and causing flaccid paralysis. Tetanus toxin cleaves Synaptobrevin in inhibitory interneurons (Renshaw cells), preventing GABA/Glycine release and causing spastic paralysis (lockjaw/tetanus).

conceptBreakdown.heading: Quantal Release of Neurotransmitters
conceptBreakdown.explanation: Neurotransmitters are released in discrete multi-molecular packets called 'Quanta', each corresponding to the exocytosis of one synaptic vesicle containing ~5,000 to 10,000 transmitter molecules.
